example.english: Let us divide the work first.

concepts.title: Suggest a shared action
concepts.explanation: The n- verb forms here mean “we”: neʾsem, we divide; neraageʿ, we review. In context they also suggest “let us”. Add sawa to mean together. Nebdaʾ be-eh? asks what to start with.

concepts.title: I will take; I am ready
concepts.explanation: Haakhod is a useful future chunk: “I will take”. For readiness a man says gahez, a woman gahza. No separate present-tense “am” is needed. Add mesh before the adjective for “not ready”.

lessons.title: Először elolvasom
lessons.subtitle: October 10, 2026 · First I read it
objectives: Find and read a short instruction.

readings.title: A guide for testing agents · October 9 publication

sentences.text: A Microsoft új útmutatót adott ki.
sentences.english: Microsoft published a new guide.
The guide is about testing AI tools.
It helps find the cause of errors.
Anna: Where is the guide?
Bence: Here it is, on the screen.
Anna: First I read the instruction.
Bence: Is there an example in it?

sentences.text: Anna: Igen, itt egy rövid példa.
sentences.english: Anna: Yes, here is a short example.
Bence: I will try it afterwards.
Anna: Which step is difficult?

sentences.text: Bence: Ez a lépés. Nem értem.
sentences.english: Bence: This step. I do not understand.
Anna: Let us look at the example!
Bence: Now I understand.
Anna: Is the first task finished?

sentences.text: Bence: Igen, kész. Jöhet a következő.
sentences.english: Bence: Yes, it is finished. Next one, please.

concepts.title: First read, then try
concepts.explanation: Először means first; utána means afterwards. Put either at the start to order actions. Elolvasom and kipróbálom refer to a specific object: I read it through; I try it out. With an explicit object use -t: az utasítást, a példát.

concepts.title: Describe a step
concepts.explanation: Melyik lépés nehéz? asks which step is difficult. Ez a lépés nehéz identifies this step. Nem before the adjective makes it negative. There is no separate “is” in these third-person present descriptions.
